Indikator 5y measures the proportion of acute surgical patients (without perforation, ischemia, or bleeding) who are operated on within six hours of admission [^src1]. The national standard requires that at least 90% of these patients meet this timeframe [^src1]. However, the data from 2023 reveals a systemic failure to meet this target across all Danish regions and hospitals, with every single entity recording a fulfillment rate of 0% ("Nej") against the >= 90% threshold [^src1].

Nationally, only 14.7% of the 2,010 eligible patients were operated on within the six-hour window [^src1]. Among the five regions, [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] performed best with 19.9% of patients treated within the timeframe, followed by [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] at 16.2% [^src1]. Conversely, [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] and [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] trailed at the bottom with 9.0% and 9.6%, respectively [^src1]. [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] recorded a rate of 10.6% [^src1]. 

At the hospital level, there is a massive outlier: Bornholms Hospital achieved a rate of 68.4% (13 out of 19 patients), which is drastically higher than the national average and any other institution, though it still falls short of the 90% target [^src1]. Excluding this outlier, the highest-performing hospitals were Bispebjerg og Frederiksberg Hospitaler and Hospitalsenhed Midt, both at 25.2% [^src1]. The lowest rates were recorded at Nykøbing F Sygehus (0.0%), Amager og Hvidovre Hospital (3.2%), and Regionshospitalet Gødstrup (5.2%) [^src1]. Because the provided data consists of only a single snapshot from 2023, no longitudinal trends regarding improvement or decline can be established.
